newsitem.title: UK: Stg wobbles, small rate rise prompts profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Stg wobbles, small rate rise prompts profit-taking.

text.p: Sterling was close to session lows in European afternoon trading after a rise of just 25 basis points in UK interest rates prompted traders to book profits on long positions.
The pound initially dropped on news that official interest rates had been raised to 6.75 percent amid disappointment that the central bank had not opted for a more aggressive 1/2 point increase.
The pound dropped close to the 2.95 mark level soon after the announcement but recovered to 2.9750 - within a whisker of Wednesday's six-year high - before resuming its slide back to session lows.
Dealers said the pound's seesaw movements reflected a degree of uncertainty about whether it will continue its relentless rally of about 30 percent against the mark since last August.

"There is a number of people who now see a top in sterling/mark," said a trader at a U.S. bank. "But the market is still mainly bullish for a rise above 3.00 marks, and dealers are keen to buy it back at lower levels," he said.

The weakness of dollar/mark also weighed on sterling, dealers said. The dollar shed a pfennig after Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said the dollar's correction against the mark was now over and that the central bank wanted the mark to be strong in the run-up to European monetary union.
A shake-out in dollar/mark rate is likely to put a brake on sterling too.
The prospect of further UK interest rate rises should remain supportive for the pound as rates are likely to remain low in continental Europe where sluggish economic growth persists.
In Britain, analysts expect more rate rises in order to rein in robust consumer spending, fuelled by massive windfall profits for consumers from building societies converting into banks.

"Sterling is well supported by the interest rate rise, and investors are looking for further gains," said Neil MacKinnon, chief economist at Citibank. "The pound will continue to be supported by favourable interest rate differentials."
At 1440 GMT the pound traded at 2.9523/33 compared with 2.9640 before the rate news and down from 2.9671/81 in late European trading on Wednesday.
Against the dollar, sterling stuck to a range of less than a cent, trading at $1.6872/82 compared with around $1.69 before the rate rise and $1.6844/49 at the previous European close.
